oneLiner: Arguably the best operating metrics in software (Rule of 40 = 155, +93% growth at $8B scale) attached to the most expensive multiple in large-cap software (~50x forward sales), now converting prototypes into production hardware programs.
thesis: AIP is winning the enterprise agentic-AI land grab: US commercial +149% YoY with 157% net dollar retention and accelerating sequential growth.

Government is an annuity with upside, and it is moving from prototype to production: the $10B/10-year Army Enterprise Agreement, NATO Maven purchases, NGC2, Golden Dome, and on Sep 1, 2026 the Army moving TITAN into its production phase.
The ontology layer creates deep switching costs: data, logic and actions bound into operational workflows; 157% NDR is the evidence.
Margins are already elite: 62% adjusted operating margin and $4.5-4.7B of FCF guided for FY2026. The entire question is what multiple to pay.

latestQuarter.label: Q2 2026 (reported Aug 3, 2026)
points: Adjusted operating margin 62%; GAAP operating margin 47%; GAAP net margin 55% (including SpaceX marks).
Government $990M (+79%), US government $809M (+90%); US commercial $764M (+149% YoY, +28% sequential).
Guide raised: FY2026 revenue $8.15B (+82%); US commercial above $3.42B (+134%); adjusted FCF $4.5-4.7B; Q3 ~$2.16B.

segments: Government ~51% of revenue: Army Enterprise Agreement, NATO Maven, TITAN, allied defense.
Commercial ~49%, with US commercial (+149%) the growth engine on AIP adoption; an expanded PwC alliance is the newest enterprise distribution channel.
competitive: Enterprise AI platforms: Databricks, Snowflake Cortex and Microsoft Fabric target the same data and AI budgets.
Defense tech: Anduril is simultaneously partner and rival - the two split the Sep 2026 TITAN production orders ($127M to Palantir, $65M to Anduril) after jointly winning Army NGC2 work in July.
The big consultancies compete for AI-implementation budgets; Palantir's forward-deployed model positions it as software rather than billable hours, and the PwC alliance co-opts one of them.
C3.ai has faded as a serious threat.
moat: The ontology layer binding an institution's data, logic and actions creates switching costs once operational workflows run through Foundry and AIP. In government: decades of accreditations, classified deployments and contract vehicles newcomers cannot replicate quickly - and with TITAN, a hardware delivery program that embeds Palantir in the Army's deep-sensing architecture rather than alongside it.
risks: Valuation: roughly 67x trailing EV/sales is about 150% above its own 10-year median; any growth wobble is severely punished.

Insider selling remains relentless: reports of an $86M CEO sale in the same month as the TITAN award follow ~$54M in May 2026 and more than $250M by insiders in late 2025, against 34 sells and zero buys over five years (reported).
Bear scrutiny of accounting: Michael Burry has publicly renewed a bearish position citing accounting practices and valuation (reported).
Government dependency: ~51% of revenue is tied to US and allied budgets; a continuing resolution or budget fight hits the biggest segment.
Law of large numbers: +93% on an $8B base is unprecedented, and 2027 comparisons get brutal.
Hardware programs like TITAN carry delivery, integration and schedule risk that pure software does not - eight systems over 18 months is an execution commitment.
Stock-based compensation keeps GAAP margins (47%) well below adjusted (62%).
catalysts: US federal fiscal year-end Sept 30 award flow.
TITAN delivery milestones across the eight initial systems (four Advanced, four Basic) over the next 18 months.
Army NGC2 next-phase decision around mid-2027.
Golden Dome milestones and further NATO or allied Maven expansions.
pricedIn: Around $174-186 in early September, roughly 12-16% below the $207.52 52-week high, at approximately 82x forward earnings and 50x forward sales. To justify it, Palantir has to hold 60%+ growth for years at ~60% adjusted margins, taking $8.15B toward $25B+ by 2029-2030, which brings EV/sales toward ~17x on out-year sales. Bulls point to Q2's +93% and the fact that TITAN and NGC2 turn demos into programs of record. Bears note the market barely moved on a fresh DoD award, which is what a fully-priced stock looks like: good news is already in it.

scenarios.bear: US commercial growth halves as AIP pilots saturate and Databricks, Snowflake and Fabric win the mainstream; a 2027 budget impasse freezes government; NDR fades toward 120%. Growth of 'only' 40% forces the multiple from ~50x toward 15-20x forward sales - a 50-60% derating even with rising earnings.
scenarios.base: FY2026 lands at $8.15B (+82%); 2027 decelerates to 45-60% at ~60% adjusted margins and $4.5B+ of FCF; production programs like TITAN add durable but low-multiple revenue; the multiple compresses gradually as earnings grow into it and the stock oscillates in the established $130-210 range with earnings-driven spikes.
scenarios.bull: AI agents in production become the enterprise standard with AIP the category winner; US commercial sustains above 100% into 2027; Golden Dome, NGC2 and TITAN convert into multi-billion production programs; revenue triples by 2028-29 and growth outruns multiple compression.

valPresets.note: Even the bear preset needs 25% year-one FCF growth; the reverse DCF shows roughly 30%+ constant growth for a decade is priced in. That asymmetry is the entire PLTR debate.

sources.label: TITAN production orders split with Anduril

latestProse: Q2 2026 (reported Aug 3). Revenue $1.94B, +93% against ~$1.80B consensus; adjusted operating margin 62%, GAAP operating margin 47%. US commercial $764M, +149% YoY and +28% sequential; US government $809M, +90%. Net dollar retention 157%, up 700bp sequentially, for a Rule of 40 score of 155. Since the print, the Army moved TITAN into production on Sep 1, awarding $192M of delivery orders - $127M to Palantir USG and $65M to Anduril - covering eight initial systems, four Advanced and four Basic, over 18 months. The disclosure that matters most: 157% net dollar retention with US commercial still accelerating sequentially, because the bear case has always been that AIP land-and-expand saturates, and it has not started to.
guidanceProse: FY2026 is guided to $8.15B (+82%), US commercial above $3.42B (+134%), adjusted FCF $4.5-4.7B, and Q3 around $2.16B. At roughly 50x forward sales the guide has to keep being beaten rather than merely met - every quarter is a referendum on the multiple. The September signal is what did not happen: a fresh DoD production award and an expanded PwC alliance landed without moving the stock, which trades 12-16% below its high, while Michael Burry publicly renewed a short thesis on accounting and valuation and insiders kept selling.
